summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman with sickle cell disease was admitted for a severe pain crisis involving her limbs and joints, following weeks of worsening pain managed at home with limited success. She presented somnolent due to prior sedation but stabilized after 18 hours of rest and continuous IV pain control with Dilaudid, ketorolac, and fluids. A chest X-ray ruled out acute chest syndrome or infection, and labs showed no evidence of acute complications. Over several days, she transitioned successfully to oral hydromorphone and was discharged home in stable condition. Her hydroxyurea dose was maintained at 500 mg twice daily, considering her underlying Hepatitis C with stage III fibrosis. Follow-up was advised for pain management and hematologic care.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
